rounds.hypothesis: Exactly as diagnose read it: the CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE branch of the default `Inode::check_permission` (kernel/src/fs/vfs/fs_apis/inode.rs:585-604) applies Linux's 'executable DACs are overridable only when at least one exec bit is set' rule to every inode type, with no exemption for directories. So root's mkdir('testdir/subdir') -> check_dir_entry_mutation -> MAY_WRITE|MAY_EXEC on the mode-0444 'testdir' reduces to MAY_EXEC, finds no exec bit, and returns EACCES at line 598 before the owner/group/other checks are consulted. Adding the missing inode-type guard should let setup complete, after which the unprivileged assertion should already pass on existing machinery. Confirmed against Linux before patching: /tmp/namei.c:476-486 generic_permission() has `if (S_ISDIR(inode->i_mode))` with the comment `/* DACs are overridable for directories */`, and inside it capable_wrt_inode_uidgid(..., CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE) returns 0 with no exec-bit test of any kind; the exec-bit condition appears only on the non-directory fallthrough at 496-504.
rounds.change: One inode-type guard in `Inode::check_permission`, kernel/src/fs/vfs/fs_apis/inode.rs. The existing `if perm.may_exec()` became `if metadata.type_.is_directory() { perm -= Permission::MAY_EXEC; } else if perm.may_exec() { ...unchanged... }`. Directories therefore also drop MAY_EXEC alongside the MAY_READ|MAY_WRITE already dropped at line 588, and can no longer reach the EACCES return. The exec-bit test and its error path are byte-for-byte unchanged for every non-directory type. 7 insertions, 2 deletions, one file; no new imports, since `metadata.type_` was already read at line 582 and `InodeType::is_directory()` already exists at kernel/src/fs/file/inode_attr/type.rs:25.
rounds.outcome: green on the first round. `PATH=<osdk_bin>:$PATH VNC_PORT=3907 make run_kernel AUTO_TEST=conformance CONFORMANCE_TEST_SUITE=ltp CONFORMANCE_TEST_SELECTOR=statfs03 CARGO_OSDK=<osdk_bin>/cargo-osdk` exited 0; qemu.log reports `statfs03: pass  (0.012s)` and Passed 1 / Failed 0 / Broken 0 / Skipped 0 / Warnings 0, then `All conformance tests passed.` That matches the host LTP 20260529 baseline exactly (1/0/0/0), so the previous `statfs03.c:26: TBROK: mkdir(testdir/subdir, 0444) failed: EACCES (13)` is gone and the real assertion at statfs03.c:36 now runs and holds.

layer: VFS, above the filesystem -- the default `Inode::check_permission` in kernel/src/fs/vfs/fs_apis/inode.rs:573, which is diagnose's `owning_layer` unchanged. Re-verified in the worktree rather than taken on trust: `grep -rn 'fn check_permission' kernel/` returns that line and nothing else, so no filesystem overrides it. The hits in ramfs/fs.rs:1339-1362 and ext2/impl_for_vfs/inode.rs:279-294 are `self.check_permission(...)` *calls* into the trait default, not definitions -- which is why one guard here fixes all six filesystems at once and patching ramfs or ext2 would have left the identical defect reachable through every other one.
generalizes: The guard is on the inode's *type*, and on nothing the test supplies. It never mentions mode 0444, the MAY_WRITE|MAY_EXEC mask mkdir happens to request, or EACCES, so there is no input this test provides that the branch is tuned to; every directory reaches it identically for any mode and any R/W/X mask. Three of the callers diagnose named are fixed beyond this test, and the test only exercises the second: resolver.rs:558 lookup_at_path asks MAY_EXEC on every path component, so root can now traverse *any* directory lacking exec bits, which repairs every path-taking syscall under a mode-0444 or mode-0600 directory rather than just mkdir; path/mod.rs:268 check_dir_entry_mutation now lets root's mkdir/rmdir/unlink/rename/link/symlink/create work inside such a directory; and access.rs:108 stops mis-reporting access(X_OK) on a directory for root. The callers that must not move do not move, by construction. Non-directories take the `else if` arm with its original body, so program_loader/mod.rs:124 and inode_handle.rs:46 keep the exec-bit requirement on regular files -- root still cannot exec a 0644 file, which is Linux's behaviour and was already correct. path/mod.rs:743, path/mod.rs:289, access.rs:102-105, net/socket/unix/ns/path.rs:24 and inotify.rs:95 are pure MAY_READ/MAY_WRITE, already subtracted at line 588 and untouched. The MAY_ACCESS xattr callers ramfs/fs.rs:1354 and ext2/impl_for_vfs/inode.rs:289 are unaffected because MAY_ACCESS is none of R/W/X. The unprivileged half of statfs03 is likewise untouched: the whole change lives inside the `has_dac_override_capability` branch, which is false for nobody after seteuid clears the effective set, so the EACCES the test actually asserts still comes from resolver.rs:558 -- and the run proves it, since a fix that had leaked into the unprivileged path would have turned the TBROK into a failed assertion instead of a pass. One deliberate non-change: CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH is still never consulted (diagnose's first adjacent gap), so a process holding it without CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE still gets no bypass. That is a separate missing capability, not part of this invariant, and folding it in would have widened the patch past what the stated invariant needs.
fix_summary: Exempts directories from the exec-bit precondition on CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE, so a capability holder may read, write, and search a directory whatever its permission bits, while non-directories keep the requirement that overriding execute needs at least one exec bit set. Designed against Asterinas's own abstractions rather than transplanted from Linux: the discriminant is `Metadata.type_` (inode.rs:89) tested with the existing `InodeType::is_directory()` helper, not a reconstruction of Linux's `S_ISDIR(inode->i_mode)` raw-mode masking, and the fix keeps Asterinas's shape of pre-emptively *subtracting* granted bits from `perm` and falling through to the shared owner/group/other checks, instead of importing generic_permission()'s structure of acl_permission_check-first with capability fallback and an early `return 0`. The two structures coincide here because once all of MAY_READ|MAY_WRITE|MAY_EXEC are subtracted, the remaining `Permission` bits (MAY_ACCESS, MAY_OPEN, MAY_APPEND, MAY_CHDIR, MAY_NOT_BLOCK -- permission.rs:9-16) are tested by none of the mode checks at inode.rs:606-625, so the function returns Ok(()), which is exactly Linux's `return 0` for the directory case. Keeping Asterinas's structure also keeps the diff to one guard in one function; the alternative of restructuring check_permission to mirror generic_permission would have rewritten the whole function to reach the same observable behaviour.
